_purpose: Pinned validation reference numbers. Analysis compares runs against these instead of memory. Update only with new measured evidence; every value carries provenance.
_baseline: v0.0.12 (b55025b). Behavior identical to v0.0.11 in all previously-validated regimes (fetch-identical proof), so v0.0.11 reference numbers carry over.
_provenance_note: Values distilled from the 2026-07 testing campaign (kickoff doc post-v0.0.12). Runs before the repeat-surface fix (pre-b55025b adl builds, incl. 2026-07-10 30cap) are bugged-build artifacts: never reference their video analysis.

constants.present_card: EVGA XR1 Pro HDMI capture card, 60Hz, adapter 1
constants.adaptive_lag_engages_when: source period > present period / 1.25 (includes 120cap x2 FG = 60 real base)

global_caveats.content_metronome: Standard ufo content = testufo.com/framerates-versus playing a 60.000fps clip on the 59.98Hz monitor: player resyncs every ~50s. Good decode days: 1 dupe frame/cycle. Bad days: ~12-frame bursts over ~2s. The historical '4-5 dupe floor' at 60->60 IS this metronome; true relay floor ~= 0.
global_caveats.relay_beat_repeat: ~1 pick=repeat per ~50s = present-clock vs source-clock beat (59.98 vs 60). Exists in every mode with unlocked clocks. Not a defect.
global_caveats.same_day_ab: Content-burst severity tracks browser decode health. Cross-build DUPE comparisons are valid ONLY as same-day A/B pairs.
global_caveats.reverse_instrument: Needs directional content; sky/map segments false-positive.
global_caveats.stride_py: Repeat carry-forward assumption CORRECT for v0.0.12+ builds; WRONG for pre-fix adl logs.
global_caveats.jitter_tails: Present-jit p99 swings with desktop state (measured 571us and 1014us same config, different days). Same-day pairing required for jit comparisons too.
global_caveats.desktop_bracketing: Logs ALWAYS begin and end with desktop/loading content at the desktop refresh rate (game launch and quit). At sub-rate -src configs this produces ring-window lines and rate-mismatch noise in the head/tail. Exclude head and tail from all counts by default; only in-regime gameplay/content windows are scored.

log_format.temporal_line_v12: temporal dl= tgt= before=(d) after= w= pick= jit= pdt=
log_format.temporal_line_phase_pull: adds pull=<us> (append-only); effective latency = lag + pull, SUM both fields

30cap_x1_t_60_adl_kcd.ring_window_note: at sub-rate -src configs, uncapped UI bursts (dialogs/menus) lap the 8-slot ring while lag exceeds burst-rate ring depth -> transient 'older than ring window' lines; expected, -ring 16 is the cure if visible

120cap_x2_t_vsync_adl_kcd.dupes: content-dominated both builds; the matching 1:45-2:11 clusters were map open/close performed in BOTH runs (controlled); relay-attributable = scattered beat singles
120cap_x2_t_vsync_adl_kcd.map_lesson: NO map/menu flips mid-run in future tests (confuses dupe data); 120cap map A/V result: lag stayed flat 20.8ms through 21s map, one +4ms 1s blip - batch-start EMA is burst-immune by construction
120cap_x2_t_vsync_adl_kcd.latency_delta_vs_base: +4ms constant, ACCEPTED by design (T10: constant offset)
120cap_x2_t_vsync_adl_kcd.in_regime_rates: repeats/min in-regime: ~24-32 across all builds (content/dip variance, corner is not gate-sensitive: ring carries ~61.7fps > present); no-after/min: ~16-23 with adequate lag vs ~68 at bare present-period lag. ALWAYS compare in-regime rates, never whole-log totals (head/tail desktop segments dominate totals)
